newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten promises to help Hong Kong's future leader.
newsitem.headline: Patten promises to help Hong Kong's future leader.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Wednesday congratulated the man who will succeed him when the British colony returns to China next year and promised him "all necessary assistance" in the months ahead.
Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa was overwhelmingly voted in as leader-in-waiting by a 400-hundred strong, China-assembled electoral college on Wednesday.
"I wish Mr Tung every success in his endeavour and I have congratulated him personally." Patten said in a statement.
"The government is committed to providing all necessary assistance to Mr Tung to help him in his preparations for assuming the office of Chief Executive on July 1, 1997.
"We stand ready to discuss with Mr Tung the level and type of assistance he may require," he said.
Tung resigned from Patten's inner cabinet of advisers in order to contend for the post of chief executive-designate, as the post-colonial governorship will be known.
Tung will take the helm when Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, is returned to China at midnight on June 30 next year under the terms of a 1984 Sino-British treaty.

Beijing has declared that Hong Kong will become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China, permitted considerably autonomy and allowed to maintain its capitalist way of life for 50 years under paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's one country, two systems policy.
